stem: A software vendor publishes installation packages through a third-party content-delivery network. The packages are intentionally public, but customers must be able to detect tampering and verify that a package was approved by the vendor even if the delivery network is compromised. Which control BEST supports the requirement?
decision_point: use digital signing to verify publisher authenticity and artifact integrity independently of the distribution channel
misconceptions: confidentiality is required for public software authenticity
TLS from a CDN alone proves publisher approval
hash without authenticated source proves who approved a file

originality.authoring_note: Original public-software distribution scenario distinguishing authenticity/integrity from confidentiality and delivery-channel security.

options: Encrypt every package with a shared secret so customers cannot see it before installation

Digitally sign approved packages and distribute the verification trust material through an appropriate trusted mechanism so customers can verify integrity and publisher authenticity independently of the CDN
Rely only on HTTPS between customers and the CDN because transport encryption proves the vendor approved every object the CDN serves
Publish an unauthenticated hash beside each package on the same potentially compromised CDN and treat that as proof of publisher identity
explanation: A digital signature can support integrity and authenticity of a public artifact independently of the transport path; it can also contribute to nonrepudiation when the surrounding key, identity, and process controls are sound.
distractor_rationales: Confidentiality is not the stated goal because the packages are intentionally public, and a shared secret would create difficult distribution and attribution problems.

A digital signature can support integrity and authenticity of a public artifact independently of the transport path; it can also contribute to nonrepudiation when the surrounding key, identity, and process controls are sound.
TLS protects a connection to the CDN, but a compromised or malicious distribution endpoint could still serve an unauthorized artifact unless the artifact itself is verifiable.
A hash can detect change only when the expected hash is itself obtained authentically; publishing both through the same compromised channel does not establish publisher identity.

stem: A replacement monitoring platform has passed functional and security testing, but operations has not validated alert routing, backup ownership, support runbooks, on-call training, or the plan to retire the old platform and its service accounts. The project wants to declare the new system fully transitioned because the software is technically ready. What is the BEST lifecycle decision?
decision_point: treat operational readiness, validated integration, sustainment, and retirement as part of system lifecycle transition
misconceptions: old-system retirement is unrelated to new-system deployment
operations training can wait until after production failure

originality.authoring_note: Sibling of the changed-requirement lifecycle item but tests operational transition/sustainment and retirement readiness rather than requirement traceability.

options: Declare transition complete because application testing is the only lifecycle gate that matters after development

Complete and validate operational integration and sustainment readiness—including alert routing, backups, runbooks, ownership/training—and execute a controlled retirement plan for the old platform and credentials
Keep both platforms and all service accounts indefinitely so no retirement decision is required
Move to production immediately and write support procedures only if the first incident reveals a gap
explanation: A system lifecycle extends beyond development testing. Controlled transition includes operational integration, ownership, monitoring, recovery, support readiness, and planned retirement of replaced assets and trust relationships.
distractor_rationales: Technical test completion does not prove that the system can be safely operated, supported, recovered, or integrated into organizational processes.

A system lifecycle extends beyond development testing. Controlled transition includes operational integration, ownership, monitoring, recovery, support readiness, and planned retirement of replaced assets and trust relationships.
Indefinitely retaining obsolete systems and credentials increases attack surface, cost, and ambiguity rather than completing transition.
Waiting for production failure to define support and recovery responsibilities creates avoidable operational and security risk.

stem: A safety-critical controller has explicit security requirements that unauthorized firmware changes must be detected before execution and that loss of one processing node must not interrupt the safety function. The selected control baseline includes MFA for administrators and disk encryption but reviewers cannot show how either requirement is fully satisfied. What should the architect do NEXT?
subtopics: derive controls from system security requirements
decision_point: trace each security requirement to controls and assurance evidence that actually satisfy the required property
misconceptions: a generic baseline proves every requirement is covered
MFA solves firmware authenticity and node failure
requirement gaps can be accepted implicitly

originality.authoring_note: Sibling of the baseline-tailoring item but tests requirement-by-requirement control coverage and assurance evidence for firmware integrity and fault tolerance.

options: Keep the baseline unchanged because selecting recognized controls proves all system requirements are satisfied
Trace the firmware-integrity and availability requirements to specific preventive/detective/resilience controls and verification evidence, adding or tailoring controls where coverage is missing
Remove the requirements because MFA and encryption are generally strong security controls
Declare the requirements met if the project manager accepts the control list without technical or assurance evidence
explanation: Control selection should be demonstrably connected to system security requirements. Each required property needs appropriate controls and evidence that the design can satisfy it; generic control strength is not a substitute for traceable coverage.
distractor_rationales: A respected baseline is a starting point, not proof that every system-specific requirement is covered in the actual architecture.

Control selection should be demonstrably connected to system security requirements. Each required property needs appropriate controls and evidence that the design can satisfy it; generic control strength is not a substitute for traceable coverage.
MFA and disk encryption address different threats and do not inherently provide firmware-execution integrity or processing-node fault tolerance.
Management acceptance can address residual risk through governance, but it does not transform unverified controls into evidence that explicit requirements are technically met.

stem: A quarterly security dashboard marks access reviews, backups, awareness training, and disaster-recovery preparation as green because each process owner emailed 'completed.' A sample later shows terminated accounts still active, several backups never restored successfully, and the DR contact list is obsolete. What is the BEST assessment improvement?
decision_point: replace completion self-attestation with objective evidence and outcome-oriented measures that validate security-process effectiveness
misconceptions: process-owner attestation is always sufficient evidence
green dashboards should not be challenged by sampling

originality.authoring_note: Original security-process evidence scenario contrasting self-reported completion with sampled objective evidence and outcome measures.

options: Continue using process-owner completion emails because management reporting should rely on trust rather than verification

Define evidence requirements and meaningful KPIs/KRIs, collect artifacts such as review approvals and account changes, verify backup restores and DR readiness, and sample/test results so the dashboard reflects effectiveness rather than activity alone
Remove the negative sample results from the dashboard so historical metrics remain comparable
Measure only how quickly process owners submit their completion emails because timeliness is the most important security outcome
explanation: Security process data should provide credible evidence of both execution and effectiveness. Objective artifacts, outcome-oriented metrics, and validation/sampling can reveal control failures that completion self-attestation hides.
distractor_rationales: Owner attestation can be one input, but the scenario demonstrates that it did not provide sufficient evidence of actual control outcomes.

Security process data should provide credible evidence of both execution and effectiveness. Objective artifacts, outcome-oriented metrics, and validation/sampling can reveal control failures that completion self-attestation hides.
Suppressing contradictory evidence defeats the purpose of assessment and produces misleading management information.
Submission speed is an administrative activity metric and does not show whether accounts were removed, backups were restorable, training changed behavior, or recovery plans were current.
